hints.content:
We can use the Pythagorean Theorem to find $x$ and $y$ in the picture below:



[[☃ image 1]]

Then the length we are looking for will be $x+3+y$.

The right triangle on the left side has a base of x kilometers, a height of three kilometers, and a hypotenuse of five kilometers. The right triangle on the right side has a base of y kilometers, a height of three kilometers, and a hypotenuse of seven kilometers.

hints.content: The equation for the Pythagorean Theorem is $a^2 + b^2  = c^2$, where $a$ and $b$ are the lengths of the two legs of the triangle, and $c$ is the length of the hypotenuse.

Applying the theorem to the triangle on the left we have:

$
\begin{align}
x^2 +3^2&= 5^2\\\\
x^2 &= 5^2-3^2\\\\
x^2 &= 25-9\\\\
x^2 &=16\\\\
x&=4
\end{align}
$

Applying the theorem to the triangle on the right the we have:

$
\begin{align}
y^2 +3^2&= 7^2\\\\
y^2 &= 7^2-3^2\\\\
y^2 &= 49-9\\\\
y^2 &=40\\\\
y&=\sqrt{40}\\\\
y&\approx 6.3
\end{align}
$

So the distance we are looking for is $4 + 3+6.3 =13.3$

To the nearest tenth of a kilometer, the plane traveled $13.3$ kilometers horizontally.
